title: Sharp Separable Effects When a Persistent Binary Frailty Violates Dismissible-Component Conditions
banked_reason: Sound exact results, but D0.5 assessed incremental novelty with paper_score_ceiling 5.9 below the field threshold 7.4; the attempted all-cell K1 Bayes-coherence classification left residual observable cells unclassified.

the required finite quantifier-free all-cell partition and whole-risk-set factorization/infeasibility certificates did not land

proof_attempt_summary: The run proved exact shared-frailty compatibility and a constructive causal-law lift, compact semialgebraic component computation, a corrected observable Gamma=1 compatibility theorem, and a robust K=1 strict gap with endpoints 207/500 versus 63/160. It then attempted the field-critical all-cell K1 Bayes-coherence elimination, obtaining posterior-weight reductions, boundary cells, a sufficient equality regime, and a strict open cell, but not the complete observable sign-cell classification. General connectedness remains open, so the sound result was banked at incremental novelty.
tldr: The paper sharply characterizes off-diagonal separable risks when all departures from marginal dismissible-component restrictions arise from one treatment-independent persistent binary frailty. It proves an exact finite polynomial compatibility theorem with a constructive four-assignment FFRCISTG lift, compact semialgebraicity and exact component computation, and inclusion in a precisely declared history-rectangular relaxation. At the smallest positive horizon it proves a robust strict gap---shared lower endpoint \(207/500\) versus rectangular lower endpoint \(63/160\) at the rational center law, with an explicit rational open neighborhood. At \(\Gamma=1\), the shared class is nonempty exactly when the observable common-state condition \(C_L(P^{\mathrm{obs}})\) holds; under splice positivity the compatible face collapses to the ordinary separable g-formula, whereas failure of \(C_L\) gives the empty set. Without splice positivity the theorem retains an exact residual projection and makes no interval claim. A complete observable classification of equality with the rectangular relaxation and general finite-tree connectedness remain explicit research questions.
gap: Published separable-effect theory point identifies off-diagonal risks when dismissible-component conditions hold and offers sensitivity functions when they fail, but it does not characterize the histories jointly attainable when one persistent latent cause generates both diagonal arms and all four component assignments. Generic marginal or longitudinal sensitivity bounds allow more local freedom and need not be sharp for this scientific model.
fill: It seeks an iff compatibility theorem and causal-law lift, certified semialgebraic computation, an exact relation to a declared rectangular relaxation, a minimal robust strictness witness, an answer on connectedness, and exact \(\Gamma=1\) and \(\Gamma\to\infty\) boundary behavior.
